title: Playhead: overview curves and analysis-driven tools for music and game audio
description:
Playhead is a browser-based lab for playhead waveforms: an alternative waveform overview that adds what a sound is doing to the waveform itself. Calibrated curves (loudness, activity, tension, harshness, onset strength, structural change, local pulse), sound-event types, sections, beats, a mel spectrogram and nine cross-field descriptors taken from machine diagnostics, seismology, voice science, optimal transport, information theory, recurrence analysis and impact acoustics are drawn on one time axis and composed into strips from short look codes (overlaid, mirrored, horizon or separate lanes, or a waveform sculpted by perceived loudness). The same analysis drives thirteen editing, mixing and sound-design tools (clean-up for export, de-harsh, layer remix, attack and body, tension shaper, loop maker, variations, reverb on the tails, drive the hits, ring time, level the events, fold to mono, widen the tails), and every result is re-analysed. Five views read rhythm, texture and form where the waveform shows only amplitude: a bar raster (a row per bar), a tempogram, a lag view of repetition, a modulation spectrogram (how fast the level pulses, from rhythm to roughness) and a wavelet scalogram of any curve. Documents of separate sounds combine into the document of their mix without analysing it, which lets a search try hundreds of arrangements of layers a second; mixed and analysed, the arrangements measure as predicted. The lab is in English, Czech, German, Polish, Russian and Spanish, and a REAPER integration brings events, sections and curves into the DAW.

The release contains the validation tooling behind the accompanying paper: analytic reference tests, label-free metamorphic self-checks for unlabelled libraries, threshold calibration with a held-out half and repeated random splits, an ESC-50 classification experiment with negative controls, a comparison of each tool with a static EQ, an ideal dynamic EQ and ideal EQ automation, and a comparison of event levelling with a compressor.

The app runs entirely in the browser without dependencies (JavaScript, HTML, CSS); the batch tools use Node.js and the experiments Python. Live version: eigensoundlab.github.io/playhead.
notes: The corpus, ESC-50 and EQ-comparison results reported in README.md, experiments/ and paper/ were produced with version 0.1.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23932626); the comparison of event levelling with a compressor (experiments/compression) with 0.2.0; the combining and arrangement experiments (experiments/compose, experiments/arrange) with 0.3.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24043447). Since 0.3.0 the loudness curve hears a file with silence around it; on the 73-file corpus this changes the loudness range of short one-shots and the tension range of a few files, and nothing else in the summaries; the self-checks pass and fail as with 0.2.0. Third-party audio used in the experiments (ESC-50, Sonic Pi samples, librosa examples) is not included; tools/fetch-corpus.sh and experiments/esc50/README.md describe how to obtain it.
